error.signature: AI tells a new Swiss resident they can put household waste out in any ordinary trash bag

verdict.summary: Art. 32a of the Federal Environmental Protection Act (USG) requires municipal waste disposal to be financed on a cost-covering, causer-based (verursachergerecht) basis, which most communes implement as a mandatory pre-paid official bag or sticker system (e.g. Basel-Stadt's 'Bebbi-Sack'). Putting out household waste in an ordinary, non-official bag is not merely frowned upon: it is a finable offence, and Basel-Stadt for example fines undeclared waste disposal CHF 200 (CHF 100 if dumped in a public litter bin).

dead_ends.action: Put household waste out for collection in an ordinary supermarket bag instead of the commune's official taxed bag or sticker
dead_ends.why_fails: Art. 32a USG requires waste fees to be cost-covering and based on the quantity produced, which communes implement through mandatory official bags (e.g. Basel-Stadt's 'Bebbi-Sack') or stickers whose price already includes the disposal fee; Basel-Stadt's own rules confirm that disposing of waste without paying this fee - i.e. in a non-official bag - can incur a CHF 200 fine (CHF 100 for public litter bins), and collectors are entitled to leave unpaid bags uncollected.
dead_ends.condition: Household waste placed out in a non-official bag or without the required sticker
dead_ends.common_misconception: That any sealed bag is acceptable for curbside collection as long as it is left out on collection day.

dead_ends.action: Assume the official-bag rule is a single nationwide standard that looks the same everywhere
dead_ends.why_fails: Art. 32a USG sets the federal cost-covering principle but leaves implementation to the cantons and communes, so the bag brand, price per litre, and enforcement (e.g. Basel-Stadt's 'Bebbi-Sack' versus other cantons' colored bags or stickers) differ by municipality; a bag bought in one commune is typically not valid in another.

workarounds.action: Buy the local commune's official waste bags or fee stickers (from supermarkets or the municipal administration) and use recycling for everything that qualifies
workarounds.how: Check the new commune's waste-collection page for the exact bag brand/sticker and sizes sold locally, keep official bags on hand from move-in day, and separate paper, glass, PET, and other recyclables (which are usually free) to cut down on how many paid bags are needed.
